text:
Maya: heads up — ran adaptive-window patch on canary, saw weird tail behavior
Jordan: specifics?
Maya: p95 jumped 90ms during 30s window while throughput steady
Ravi: did coalescing rate change? could be more singletons
Maya: coalesce_rate down 22%, singletons up. logs show many tentative slots timing out
Tess: tentative slots? remind me of current heuristic
Maya: window_ms=25, tentative_timeout=20ms, admit if occupancy>=3 else cancel
Jordan: sounds like timeout too aggressive for some clients
Ravi: we could try occupancy hysteresis: require occupancy>=3 for confirm, but allow confirm if occupancy>=2 for consecutive windows
Tess: that reduces churn but increases latency for bursts
Maya: another axis: eviction_budget per-tenant. once budget exhausted, temporarily cap tentative slots
Jordan: eviction_budget seems promising to avoid thrash from noisy tenants
Ravi: fairness: if tentative slots don't count, tenants could game by opening many tentative requests to bump others out
Maya: counter: cap concurrent tentative per-tenant and penalize repeated cancellations in fairness ledger
Tess: telemetry needs: tentative_attempts, tentative_cancels, hysteresis_state, eviction_budget_remaining
ops-bot: note: canary deployed to r-7 with feature flag adaptive_window=true
Jordan: rollout plan: ramp flag from 0%->10%->50% over 6h with alert on eviction_budget>baseline*1.3
Maya: quick patch idea: when cancelling tentative, emit a short backoff for that tenant (exp backoff ms)
Ravi: pseudo:
```
if tentative_cancel: tenant.backoff = min(tenant.backoff*2, max_backoff)
else tenant.backoff = base
```
Tess: also add trace id in logs: reservation_id -> batch_id -> eviction_id
Maya: agree. I'll open RFC titled "soft-reservations + eviction budgets" with state machine sketch
Jordan: add a section about long-term: ML classifier to predict coalesce probability per-request
Ravi: ok. if RFC lands today I can prototype metrics dashboards
Maya: thanks folks, will post RFC link here once created :thumbsup:
